Use Tier 2 architectural deepening, focused on model_design: add a jointly trained recent-history residual to SASRec’s sequence representation. Increasing sampled negatives improved macro validation HR@10 by only 0.0012, motivating a representation change rather than another denominator adjustment. The hypothesis is that the final transformer state does not consistently preserve recent item identity; the existing results do not establish this as the cause of the plateau.

At each sequence position, compute the mean of the last five nonpadding input item embeddings, including the current item and excluding future items. Project this vector into the hidden dimension and inject it into the transformer output through a learned elementwise sigmoid gate, then apply layer normalization. Use this fused representation for both ranking_loss and predict, retaining the existing tied item embeddings and learned item biases. Train the projection, gate, and transformer jointly under the existing sampled-softmax objective; this remains one network producing one candidate score.

Retain 2048 negatives from the best recorded experiment and hold prefix sampling, backbone dimensions, optimizer, training seed 42, supplied splits, and checkpoint selection fixed. Update checkpoint configuration and the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the modified architecture and loads exactly one checkpoint per category. Evaluate the atomic change using the unchanged pinned host macro validation HR@10 across all four categories, recording category results and GPU cost without assuming an improvement. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, existing runtime limits, and host-managed held-out inference; do not access hidden test files or generate a separate test submission.
